Growing up Bengali in Bangalore, one if the most fascinating dynamics to observe is the Bengali Durga Pujo committees and their shenanigans. 

People who forgot you all year would magically turn up to collect "chanda" before pujo. Public sector executives and blue collar workers (especially from BEL and BHEL near our home), school teachers, retired IISc professors, businessmen etc.

As a kid, I hated what I called the "Bangali ghetto." Most other Bengali kids my age would speak neither Bengali or Kannad, and I saw no point in hanging out with these people. But we would go - to stay in touch with our roots.

But there were highlights. In class 5 or 6, I participated in a quiz and beat even college students. That same year, I also went to an antakshari and innocentky sang the Mithun classic "Gutar gutar - chadh gaya upar re," much to the horror of the crowd.  No more Antakshari.

I remember my family fighting with a pujo committee for a Bollywood night that had nothing to do with Bengali culture. A businessman assaulting an IISc professor, by slapping him for requesting an extra rossogolla during "bhog" - there were no consequences for this attack though IISc's sizeable Bengali community boycotted that pujo for a few years.

More recently, Bangalore's oldest pujo association, with its own building, was locked up by court orders due to allegations of financial impropriety and infighting. The association split up with each faction running its mega pujo now.

I wonder how Bangalore's pujos run now. With mega corporate donations and superstar performances, it is very different from the 90s and early 2000s.
